stories.title: Masaurhi resident with 90% disability still waits for a wheelchair
stories.summary: A Masaurhi resident holding a certificate that records 90% mobility disability has repeatedly visited government offices seeking a wheelchair, Khabar Lahariya reports. Her limited mobility makes leaving home difficult, yet the available account indicates that assistance has not arrived. The responsible department's response and her application's current status are not supplied.
stories.why_it_matters: A mobility aid can determine whether a disabled person can reach health care, public services and community life. Repeated office visits impose the greatest burden on the person the welfare system is meant to support.
stories.evidence_status: Khabar Lahariya provides a ground report and cites the resident's disability certificate and search for assistance. Administrative records and an official explanation are absent.

confidence.rationale: First-hand local reporting supports the access problem, but the case has no supplied government response or documentary application trail.

coverage.rationale: This individual disability-access failure appears in one local ground report and has no wider corroboration in the collection.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh plans to move 15,613 anganwadi centres onto school campuses
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh set an August 15 target to move 15,613 anganwadi centres operating near government schools onto school premises, according to Khabar Lahariya. The relocation links early-childhood services more closely with the school network. The supplied report does not explain whether every campus has suitable rooms, sanitation or arrangements for children and workers during the move.
stories.why_it_matters: Anganwadi centres provide nutrition, preschool learning and maternal support. Moving thousands of centres could improve coordination with schools, but inadequate space or rushed implementation could disrupt services for young children.
stories.evidence_status: Khabar Lahariya supplies the number of centres, the relocation plan and its deadline. No government order, district readiness data or beneficiary response accompanies the report.

confidence.rationale: A specific local report supports the announced scale and deadline, while operational details and primary documentation remain missing.

coverage.rationale: One local source covers a large service-delivery change, with no independent implementation reporting in the collection.

stories.title: Local official reports 60 killed in South Sudan cattle raid
stories.summary: Attackers killed 60 people in a cattle raid in South Sudan, according to a local official cited by The Hindu. The country has a long history of deadly livestock raids and is also experiencing clashes between forces loyal to President Salva Kiir and armed groups loosely aligned with the opposition. Independent casualty confirmation is not supplied.
stories.why_it_matters: A raid with dozens of reported deaths could deepen displacement and retaliation in communities already exposed to political conflict. Separating local violence from the wider armed struggle is important for an effective response.
stories.evidence_status: The Hindu attributes the death toll to a local official and supplies national conflict context. No hospital records, security statement or second field report independently confirms the number killed.

confidence.rationale: The event is reported through an identified official source, but the casualty figure and perpetrators lack independent corroboration in the supplied material.

coverage.rationale: One international report covers the raid, and the security situation remains fluid.

stories.title: River erosion advances to within 10 metres of Dibrugarh flood dyke
stories.summary: Nearly a week of riverbank erosion at Thakurbari in Maijan has brought the affected edge to about 10 metres from the Dibrugarh Town Protection Dyke, EastMojo reports. Residents describe substantial land loss along the bank. The embankment protects Dibrugarh and nearby areas, but the supplied account does not state whether engineers have declared it unsafe.
stories.why_it_matters: Failure of a major flood barrier could expose a dense urban area and adjoining settlements to rapidly rising water. Immediate monitoring and reinforcement decisions matter while erosion continues close to the structure.
stories.evidence_status: EastMojo provides the reported distance to the dyke, duration of erosion and residents' accounts of land loss. No engineering inspection, water-resources department response or measured erosion series is supplied.

confidence.rationale: Specific regional reporting supports the immediate risk, while the structural condition of the dyke has not been independently documented.

coverage.rationale: The erosion is continuing and appears in one regional report, with no technical authority update in the collection.

stories.title: Bad road forces pregnant Bihar woman onto tractor journey before her death
stories.summary: A pregnant woman from the Ramnagar area of Bagaha died while being transported by tractor because poor road access prevented ordinary travel to health care, Khabar Lahariya reports. The account connects her death to gaps in both transport and medical access. Hospital records, the precise cause of death and responses from local authorities are not supplied.
stories.why_it_matters: When an unusable road blocks timely obstetric care, infrastructure failure becomes a direct health risk. The case raises urgent questions about emergency transport and referral access for remote communities in Bihar.
stories.evidence_status: Khabar Lahariya provides a local account linking the tractor journey to road conditions and reporting the woman's death en route. Medical certification, family testimony in full and official responses are unavailable.

confidence.rationale: The local report supports the transport failure and reported outcome, but the medical cause and institutional responsibility remain unverified.

coverage.rationale: One rural newsroom reports the case, with no separate health-department or roads-agency account in the supplied evidence.

stories.title: Seasonal karem greens provide monsoon income for Bundelkhand women
stories.summary: Women in Bundelkhand are earning seasonal income by gathering and selling karem, a leafy vegetable that grows after monsoon rain in fields, canals and other damp ground, Khabar Lahariya reports. Demand extends from villages to towns. The available extract describes the livelihood but does not quantify earnings, market prices or the number of women involved.
stories.why_it_matters: Small seasonal trades can provide flexible cash income where formal jobs are scarce, especially for rural women. Price stability, safe access to gathering areas and local demand determine how much the opportunity improves household finances.
stories.evidence_status: Khabar Lahariya supplies a local account of harvesting conditions, demand and women's participation. No income records, market survey or independent livelihood assessment accompanies the report.

confidence.rationale: Ground reporting supports the existence of the seasonal trade, while its scale and financial value remain undocumented.

coverage.rationale: The livelihood appears in one rural report and receives no broader economic coverage in the collection.

stories.title: Meghalaya sends 651,644 voter records to notice-and-hearing scrutiny
stories.summary: Meghalaya's Chief Electoral Officer said 651,644 electors were flagged for further review during the notice-and-hearing phase of the Special Intensive Revision. EastMojo reports that 222,786 records lacked mapping and 428,858 carried other discrepancies. Being flagged is not the same as deletion, and the supplied material does not state how many voters will ultimately remain on the roll.
stories.why_it_matters: Scrutiny affecting more than six lakh records could reshape access to the franchise before future elections. Transparent notices, accessible hearings and correction procedures are essential to prevent eligible voters from being excluded.
stories.evidence_status: EastMojo attributes the figures and categories to Chief Electoral Officer B.D.R. Tiwari. The underlying roll data, district breakdown and outcomes of individual hearings are not supplied.

confidence.rationale: An identified election official supports the scale of scrutiny, but no primary dataset or completed hearing results are available.

coverage.rationale: The revision is in its notice-and-hearing stage, and one regional desk reports the current figures.

stories.title: Prakash Raj says Bengaluru voter record was flagged during roll revision
stories.summary: Actor and former independent candidate Prakash Raj says his Bengaluru voter entry was placed in the ASDDO category during Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision, a designation covering absent, shifted, deceased, duplicate and other records. Two newsrooms report his allegation. The State's Chief Electoral Officer urged voters to verify their details, but the supplied evidence does not independently establish his final registration status.
stories.why_it_matters: A disputed entry involving a prominent former candidate draws attention to how revision categories are applied and corrected. The larger democratic issue is whether every affected voter receives clear notice and an effective appeal route.

stories.title: Supreme Court asks 19 jurisdictions to make cancer a notifiable disease
stories.summary: The Supreme Court asked 19 States and Union Territories to declare cancer a notifiable disease to support earlier detection and public-health tracking. The direction followed information that 17 of India's 36 jurisdictions had already adopted notification. The supplied report does not identify every non-compliant jurisdiction or set out the reporting system each government must establish.
stories.why_it_matters: Mandatory notification can reveal where cancer cases are rising, guide screening and improve allocation of treatment resources. Its value will depend on complete reporting, patient privacy safeguards and usable registries across States.
stories.evidence_status: The Hindu reports the Supreme Court's direction and the 17-of-36 adoption figure. The court order, jurisdiction list and implementation deadlines are not included in the supplied material.

confidence.rationale: A court report supports the direction and national count, while the primary order and implementation details remain unavailable.

coverage.rationale: The direction requires action from 19 jurisdictions and is represented by one national report in the collection.

stories.title: Allahabad High Court orders inquiry into Ghaziabad police refusal to file assault FIR
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court ordered an inquiry into senior Ghaziabad police officers, including the commissioner, after a sexual-assault complaint alleging cognisable offences did not result in an FIR. The bench noted that the complainant had to approach a magistrate and restated the police duty to register information and investigate. The underlying allegation has not been adjudicated.

stories.title: IITs and IIMs begin voluntary drug screening under national student programme
stories.summary: Selected IITs and IIMs have begun offering voluntary urine drug tests at admission under a government programme aiming to screen one million students at 170 central institutions by 2029. The framework says results must remain confidential, carry no adverse consequences and be used only for counselling. The supplied report does not describe consent procedures or early participation rates.
stories.why_it_matters: Testing tied to admission can affect privacy, stigma and trust even when formally voluntary. Clear consent, strict confidentiality and separation from discipline are necessary if the programme is to support health rather than punish students.
stories.evidence_status: The Hindu reports the programme target, institutional scope and safeguards attributed to the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre framework. The framework document, consent forms and outcome data are not supplied.

confidence.rationale: The policy design and initial institutional use are specifically reported, while implementation and student experience have not yet been independently evaluated.

coverage.rationale: The programme is beginning and seeks major expansion by 2029; one education desk covers its launch.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha passes tribunal overhaul while Opposition is absent
stories.summary: The Rajya Sabha passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill while Opposition members were absent. Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said the measure is intended to create a modern, independent and uniform tribunal system. The supplied report confirms passage in the upper house but does not describe the bill's provisions, amendments, voting record or remaining assent steps.
stories.why_it_matters: Tribunals decide disputes affecting taxation, services, regulation and individual rights. Changes to appointments, tenure or oversight could alter their independence and efficiency, making the final statutory text more important than the government's stated objective alone.
stories.evidence_status: The Hindu reports Rajya Sabha passage, the Opposition's absence and the law minister's stated purpose. The bill text and a detailed account of debate are not supplied.

confidence.rationale: Parliamentary reporting establishes the legislative stage and political circumstances, but the available evidence is insufficient to assess substantive provisions.

coverage.rationale: The bill has cleared the upper house, while its final text and completion of the legislative process require further documentation.

stories.title: Centre defends uniform hospital-rate rule despite unresolved price ranges
stories.summary: A national rule on private-hospital pricing remains before the Supreme Court. Defending the regulation, the Union Health Ministry says it is valid even though officials have not set the actual price bands because State governments disagree. Ophthalmologists challenging the measure contend that one framework cannot fairly cover specialists working in expensive metropolitan markets and those practising in smaller towns or remote areas.
stories.why_it_matters: Uniform price bands could make private care more predictable and affordable, but rates that ignore regional costs may affect service availability. The unresolved ranges leave both patients and hospitals without a clear operating standard.
stories.evidence_status: Bar & Bench describes the ministry's counter-affidavit, the challenged rule and the petitioner's regional-cost argument. The affidavit, proposed rate schedule and positions of individual States are not supplied.

confidence.rationale: Detailed court reporting supports both sides' stated positions, while the policy remains incomplete and the primary filings are unavailable.

coverage.rationale: The Supreme Court challenge continues and the government concedes that operative rate ranges have not been finalised.
